title: Bondly
description: A digital-to-physical friendship platform for adults navigating unwanted loneliness — matched by life stage, not just interests.
imageAlt: Three friends laughing together on a bench in a tulip field

metric.label: Target repeat-activity rate within 30 days, vs a 15% industry baseline.

caseStudy.subhead: A digital-to-physical friendship platform for adults (25–40) navigating unwanted loneliness. I led discovery, stress-tested my own assumptions against research, and shaped the strategy before any code was written.

problem.heading: The problem
paragraphs: 40%+ of young adults report unwanted loneliness, yet friendship apps lose 70%+ of users within three weeks — because they optimize for match volume, not the repeated, safe interactions that actually build trust.

Existing tools treat friendship like dating: 1-on-1 dates that feel like interviews, impersonal 30-person events, swipe mechanics that gamify connection — and nothing to support the jump from acquaintance to real friend.

caseStudy.researchSummary: 3 expert + 8 user interviews, a 19-person survey and 9 competitors mapped before any design work started.

hypotheses.assumption: Users struggle because they lack social skills or are introverted
hypotheses.reality: 6 of 8 interviewees were social in comfortable settings — the friction was specific to meeting new people.

hypotheses.assumption: The main barrier is finding people with shared interests
hypotheses.reality: Interests matter, but loneliness type and life stage predicted lasting connections better.

hypotheses.assumption: People prefer large events to meet many potential friends at once
hypotheses.reality: 2–4 people was the “goldilocks zone” — intimate enough for depth, not as pressured as 1-on-1.

hypotheses.assumption: Digital-first relationships can work if done right
hypotheses.reality: It works as an intro — but has to move to in-person fast, or the connection fizzles.

pullQuote.text: I'm tired of always being the one who reaches out. I need friendships where both people care.

strategy.heading: Strategy & what's next
strategy.paragraph: Small groups (2–4 people), matched by life stage and loneliness type — not just interests — with a facilitated first activity instead of a blind coffee date. Before writing product code, I designed a manual pilot to test it: 30 beta users across 3 Barcelona cohorts.

metrics.description: Target: users who attend 2+ activities in 30 days (vs a 15% industry baseline).
Target: users reporting they felt closer to new friends after activity #2.
